advice: Experiment: reuse one packed A row panel across adjacent output-column tiles. Keep the existing four FP32 ZA selectors mapped to a 2VL×2VL output tile, and process one row panel across all j tiles before moving to the next panel. For each reduction step, load the two A vectors once and use them for selectors 0 and 1 with the first B vector, then selectors 2 and 3 with the second B vector; load the two B vectors for each column tile. This is distinct from the supplied panel-pack experiments: those repack A through ZA, while this tests whether the existing full transpose can be scheduled to reuse A across j tiles without changing its layout. Hypothesis: fewer repeated A loads may improve input reuse; the larger live/reuse span may instead reduce cache efficiency. Keep increasing-k accumulation order and the existing predicated tail handling. Checks: verify only selectors 0–3 are used, all output elements are written for odd and partial tiles, n<=0 returns, and public correctness stays within 0.002. Then measure serially against fresh AC controls under the fixed benchmark; treat any score change as unverified until repeated paired measurements establish it.
risks: A vectors may already stay in cache, so reduced loads may not help; the altered loop order may worsen B locality or increase address and loop overhead. Do not infer a gain from historical battery scores or assign any joint outcome to this advice alone.
